title: Notion API Quickstart: Get a Key and Make Your First Call
snippet:
You can create an integration on any of the four plans, so your plan tier doesn't restrict your ability to build integrations, though Business and Enterprise get a higher rate limit. Price per member is the other difference that matters for this decision.
| Plan | API access per Notion docs | Price per member per month |
|---|---|---|
| Free | Included | $0 |
| Plus | Included | $10 per seat / month |
| Business | Included | Listed on Notion's pricing page |
| Enterprise | Included | Quoted by Notion sales |
Before anyone approves spend, Free lets you prove the integration works. On Plus, the $2 gap between annual and monthly billing is the cost of staying flexible, so choose monthly only if you may drop the plan soon.

At more than 3 requests per second per integration on most plans, Notion answers with a 429 and a Retry-After header, so attempting to push faster will immediately fail. Size caps apply to every request, and the pricing figures we found list per-seat charges only.
### Request rate limit and the 429 response
Fire calls without pacing and you will be throttled within seconds: Notion's [request limits page](https://developers.notion.com/reference/request-limits) sets an average of **3 requests per second on standard plans**.
Business and Enterprise workspaces get 10 requests per second, which means a bulk sync that takes an hour on a standard plan can take a third of that on Business.
For comparison, Asana, a work-management tool, allows about 150 requests per minute on its free tier.

title: Get an API Key, Rate Limits & Free Docs
snippet:
Access**Free**
Free limit**Free; ~3 req/s (180/min) per connection, 600/min on Business & Enterprise**
Cost**Free no API tier**
Auth**Bearer Token**
Format**REST · JSON**
## What is Notion API?
The Notion API turns a Notion workspace into a queryable database — pages, blocks, databases, users and comments, all reachable over REST with an integration token. It is free to call. What shapes a design is the rate limit per connection and the payload caps, including the 2,000-character limit on each rich-text field.

Notion limits requests **per connection**, averaged over a short window with some bursting allowed, and higher plans (Business and Enterprise) get a larger allowance. Database (data source) queries have their own separate limit, and the workspace as a whole has a shared budget across all its connections. Going over returns **HTTP 429** with a `rate_limited` error code and a `Retry-After` header in seconds; wait that long, or slow down and queue requests. A 529 signals overload and should be retried the same way. The current request numbers are in the free tier box on this page.
Size caps matter just as much and are part of the API's design: a single request may carry at most **1,000 block elements and 500KB**, arrays (including rich text arrays) hold at most **100 elements**, and each rich text `text.content` is limited to **2,000 characters**, as are URLs. Equation expressions are capped at 1,000 characters, and relation and people values at 100 entries per request. Too-large requests fail with HTTP 400, so split long text into several rich text objects and write big pages in chunks with append block children.

Calling the API is free. The workspace's own Notion plan governs features and history rather than API access, so an integration built against a personal workspace can behave differently once installed somewhere with different settings — worth testing before you promise a customer anything.

Is the Notion API free?
Yes, calling it costs nothing on any Notion plan. Your plan affects features and the size of the rate limit, not whether you can use the API.

What is the Notion API rate limit?
Limits apply per connection, with a higher allowance on Business and Enterprise plans and a separate limit for database queries. Exceeding them returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. The free tier box shows the current numbers.

title: Is Notion Free? The Free Plan's 1,000-Block Limit and When a Team Has to Pay (2026)
snippet:
**Yes, as of November 4, 2026, Notion has a Free plan at $0, and for one person it has no block limit. Add a second person and the Free workspace gets 1,000 blocks in total, counted from the day you signed up. Deleting content doesn't give any back. Free also caps file uploads at 5 MB, page history at 7 days and guests at 10, and its automations are buttons only. Plus costs $10 per member a month billed yearly and removes the block cap.**

| | Free | Plus ($10 per member, billed yearly) |
|---|---|---|
| Blocks | Unlimited for 1 person; 1,000 per workspace with 2+ people | Unlimited |
| File uploads | 5 MB per file | Up to 5 GB per file |
| Page history | 7 days | 30 days |
| External guests | 10 | Unlimited |
| Database automations | Buttons only | Custom database automations |
| Forms | Basic | Custom, no Notion branding |
| Notion AI | Limited trial | Limited trial |
| API speed per connection | 180 requests a minute | 180 requests a minute |
Two lines in that table surprise people. Notion AI isn't really in Plus either: the Notion Agent, AI meeting notes and enterprise search are a trial on both, and fully included from Business at $20. And the API speed is the same on Free and Plus. Notion's developer docs give Business and Enterprise 600 requests a minute per connection and every other plan 180. A solo owner on Free can connect Notion to other software at the same speed as a paid Plus team.

## Who gets Notion Plus for free?
Students and educators. Notion's pricing FAQ says the Plus plan with a 1-member limit is free with a school email address, which adds more guests, longer version history and larger uploads. It's a solo plan, so it doesn't help a team.
For everyone else, the paid ladder is $10 a member on Plus, $20 on Business and custom pricing on Enterprise, all billed yearly. Guests are free on every plan. Our [Notion pricing](https://superdupr.com/blog/notion-pricing) breakdown covers the paid plans, the API limits on an 8-person team, and what Notion AI credits cost.
